grammar_corpus.purpose: spec §20 acceptance item 7 — 'the exact served schema-v2 object AND its generated llama.cpp grammar pass the same accepted/rejected fixture corpus using only the allowed schema subset'.
grammar_corpus.what_is_executable: BOTH halves. The schema half runs a stdlib validator over the nine keywords the schema uses (jsonschema is not installed and is not installed by the script). The grammar half runs the converter's REAL output through a stdlib GBNF recognizer, itself guarded by 11 micro-grammar self-tests. No llama.cpp binary is fetched or run.
grammar_corpus.what_is_not_proven: That llama.cpp's own C++ GBNF engine agrees with this recognizer. Running the corpus through a real llama-gbnf-validator is the one remaining upgrade and needs a binary this harness deliberately does not download.
findings: maxLength IS honoured by the converter at this commit: `statement` becomes char{0,300} and `subject` char{0,40}. prompt.rs's comment calling maxLength 'decoration that G00/G03 re-enforce server-side' is stale — the bound is enforced twice, not once. The conclusion (do not rely on it) is unchanged.
The anchored sentence-ID pattern survives intact: S0, S01, s1, S99999, an unquoted S1 and a trailing-space "S1 " are all unexpressible.

The grammar is STRICTER than the schema on four cases: unknown keys, a `quote` field, byte-offset fields, and a reordered key. The schema omits `additionalProperties` by design and draft-07 defaults it to true, so JSON Schema alone would admit model-authored quote text — the exact fabrication channel the sentence-ID contract removed. Rust `deny_unknown_fields` at G00 is the authority and agrees with the grammar.

Two cases BOTH halves accept and only Rust G00 rejects: an empty `statement` (gates.rs:716 bounded_text) and `nothing_durable:true` alongside a proposal (gates.rs:680 coherence). Neither is expressible in JSON Schema or in GBNF. The corpus records them so a green run is never read as 'the schema is the contract'.

metric_definitions.note: Verbatim intent from spec §19.1. The `harness` field records whether eval/curator/score.py emits it today — four of the six do not exist yet.

generator_candidate_recall.spec: gold memory instances proposed by the generator before verification, divided by all gold memory instances
generator_candidate_recall.harness: EMITTED as `generator_candidate_recall` (scorer v2, added Wave 4b-E). The spec's definition exactly, with no proxy: the SAME one-to-one assignment post_gate_recall uses, run over every PRE-gate proposal instead of the survivors. Denominator is the 230 gold items. Per class as `per_class[t].generator_candidate_recall`; unit-level bootstrap CI as `ci.generator_candidate_recall`.
generator_candidate_recall.reads_as: The generator's own ceiling. `generator_candidate_recall - post_gate_recall` is exactly what the verifier destroyed, which is the arithmetic behind §20's 'fail closed must not degenerate into fail empty'.

verifier_false_reject_rate.spec: correctly formed labeled candidates whose gold disposition is ProposalReady or ReviewRequired but whose verifier outcome is terminal Rejected, divided by all such admissible labeled candidates; attribute every error to GateName and RejectCode
verifier_false_reject_rate.harness: EMITTED as `verifier_false_reject_rate`, but with a non-identical denominator: score.py's admissible set is 'candidates whose statement matches a gold item', because the gold set carries no disposition labels. Adjacent, not equal.
verifier_false_reject_rate.gap: The gold set must gain per-item gold dispositions before this metric means what the spec says it means.

verifier_over_escalation_rate.spec: labeled candidates whose gold disposition is ProposalReady but whose verifier disposition is ReviewRequired, divided by all gold ProposalReady candidates; attribute every escalation to GateName and ReviewCode, including OversizedEvidence separately from Synthesis
verifier_over_escalation_rate.harness: EMITTED as `verifier_over_escalation_rate` (scorer v2, added Wave 4b-E) — but with a PROXY denominator, exactly like verifier_false_reject_rate and for the same missing labels. A candidate counts as escalated when it SURVIVES and carries a non-terminal review outcome: verify.py's `flag(G3)`, or a flag verify_sid.py wrote back to the row (`synthesis`, `oversized_evidence`, `unclaimable_role`). Attribution is emitted as `over_escalation_by_code` keyed GateName:ReviewCode, with G1b:OversizedEvidence separate from G1b:Synthesis as §19.1 requires. Whole-run counts (admissible or not) are `review_flag_breakdown`.
verifier_over_escalation_rate.gap: PROXY, TWICE OVER. (1) the admissible set stands in for 'gold disposition is ProposalReady or ReviewRequired'; (2) using it here additionally assumes EVERY gold item is a gold `ProposalReady` — the gold set records memories a human judged durable, never memories a human wanted reviewed, so the spec's exact denominator does not exist and cannot be approximated from these labels. No threshold may be frozen against this number.
verifier_over_escalation_rate.correction_to_manifest_v1: manifest_version 1 stated 'its only non-terminal flag is G3 and it is 0 in every run'. True of G3, and misleading: verify_sid.py had been writing product-shaped review flags into every SID result row all along, and the qwen3-coder-30b-sid run carries 8 Synthesis and 5 UnclaimableRole. They were never read.

defer_recovery_rate.spec: deferred candidates that reach a non-deferred terminal outcome within the frozen retry/TTL policy, divided by all deferred candidates old enough to evaluate
defer_recovery_rate.harness: NOT EMITTED and not measurable by the Python harness — defer/retry lives in the Rust ledger (state.rs). Needs a run-ledger reader, not a scorer change.

defer_expiry_rate.spec: deferred candidates that reach ExpiredVisible without recovery, divided by all deferred candidates old enough to evaluate; still-pending candidates reported separately and excluded from both denominators until mature

end_to_end_candidate_recall.spec: gold memory instances that ultimately reach human review, divided by all gold memory instances
end_to_end_candidate_recall.harness: No exact equivalent. `post_gate_recall` is the de-facto stand-in (gold items claimed by a surviving proposal), but the harness has no review queue, so the two are only equal while every survivor reaches review — which is true in V1 and must be re-checked if that ever changes.

supporting_metrics_required_by_19_1: over-cap opaque-block citation count and RequireReview(OversizedEvidence) routing accuracy, with silent Pass and terminal Reject both counted as policy errors
polarity, modality, temporal, quantity, and action accuracy
false-negative rate from a predetermined audit sample
untouched approval, edit, and rejection rates
p50/p95 runtime, peak RAM, deferred backlog

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: The spec requires thresholds to be pre-registered but does not supply numbers — §19.1 and §20 name the six metrics and demand a threshold for each without setting one. Wave 4a will not invent an acceptance bar and present it as normative. A human sets these, per claim class, before the scoring run.

required_shape.rule: spec §20: 'every included claim class meets those pre-registered recall and verifier thresholds on the frozen corpus. Fail closed must not degenerate into fail empty.' A threshold set is invalid unless it constrains BOTH a floor on recall and a ceiling on false rejection for every included class.

frozen_at_next_run.anchoring_evidence: measured_baselines above. The strongest measured arm (qwen3-coder-30b-sid) sits at recall 0.209, false-reject 0.286, source_role 0.984.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: No run_meta.json records a model digest as a first-class field. The only digests recoverable are 12-hex short forms scraped from the embedded `ollama ps` sample rows, and one results dir has no ps rows at all. A pinned generator fingerprint needs the full sha256 from /api/tags at run time.
frozen_at_next_run.fix: run_bench.py should record the served digest from /api/tags into run_meta.json; the Rust provider already pins it (ProviderConfig::model_digest) and aborts on mismatch.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: run_meta.json records prompt/schema by PATH STRING only — no content hash, no git SHA, no scorer version. Reproducibility currently rests on the path not having changed underneath the result.
frozen_at_next_run.fix: stamp prompt_sha256, schema_sha256, git_sha, scorer_version, and units content_sha256 into run_meta.json.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: defer_recovery_rate and defer_expiry_rate still have no implementation anywhere in the repo. A threshold cannot be pre-registered against a metric nothing computes — and defer_expiry_rate is the terminal-loss counterweight §19.1 calls out by name, so this is the most consequential of the remaining gaps, not the smallest.
frozen_at_next_run.fix: Both need a reader over the Rust curator ledger (state.rs CuratorLedger) and cannot come from the Python harness at all: defer and retry are Rust-side state and the harness has no run clock. Neither can be evaluated without a deferral cohort matured under this manifest's exact retry_and_ttl_policy (3 attempts / 14-day TTL / [1,6,24] h backoff / 48 h grace); still-pending candidates are reported separately and excluded from both denominators until mature.
frozen_at_next_run.resolved_in_v2: generator_candidate_recall and verifier_over_escalation_rate are now implemented — see metric_definitions. verifier_over_escalation_rate remains threshold-ineligible on the proxy grounds recorded there, so implementing it did not remove a blocker; it removed an excuse for not looking.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: The gold set labels statements and evidence, not dispositions. verifier_false_reject_rate and verifier_over_escalation_rate are both defined against a gold ProposalReady/ReviewRequired label that does not exist yet.
The 58-unit set is the DEV set by its own README and has been scored against repeatedly. A frozen labeled corpus for acceptance must be held out.
§19.1 requires both; neither the Python harness nor the Rust run audit records peak RSS today. Latency p50/p95 IS recorded.

untouched approval/edit/rejection rates, review time and queue burden are only observable once a human uses the review queue on real proposals. They belong to the Phase D observation window, not to a corpus score.
